title: The common feature of leukemia-associated IDH1 and IDH2 mutations is a neomorphic enzyme activity converting alpha-ketoglutarate to 2-hydroxyglutarate
central_claims: Cancer-associated IDH1 and IDH2 mutants acquire neomorphic activity converting alpha-ketoglutarate to R-2-hydroxyglutarate; AML samples with these mutations accumulate 2HG.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: The common feature of leukemia-associated IDH1 and IDH2 mutations is a neomorphic enzyme activity converting alpha-ketoglutarate to 2-hydroxyglutarate
source_manifest.finding: Independent biochemical experiments and primary AML samples reproduce mutant IDH2 2HG production and mutant-associated elevation in patient samples; exact effect sizes differ.

source_manifest.title: The oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate activates the mTOR signalling pathway.
source_manifest.finding: Mutant IDH1/2 and 2HG activate mTOR via KDM4A/DEPTOR in tested systems, extending the neomorphic enzyme finding.

source_manifest.title: Enasidenib in mutant IDH2 relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia.
source_manifest.finding: A phase1/2 trial of selective mutant-IDH2 inhibition produced responses in refractory AML; abstract read, not a randomized efficacy comparison.
